recognize_zh: 低倍血液抹片可見紅血球普遍排成長鏈狀的疊錢狀（rouleaux），提示血中有大量單株免疫球蛋白；視野中央僅一顆深藍色單核細胞，解析度不足以確認是否為漿細胞。
features: Low-power field dominated by prominent rouleaux formation with red cells in long branching chains
Single small round cell with intensely basophilic cytoplasm near the center; nuclear detail not resolvable
Faint bluish background staining can accompany increased serum protein
Scattered platelets; very few leukocytes in this field
Image resolution limits assessment of eccentric nucleus or perinuclear hof
describe_en: Low-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows marked rouleaux formation, with red cells stacked in long, branching chains across the field, suggesting a high concentration of serum immunoglobulin. A single cell with deeply basophilic cytoplasm is present centrally, but the magnification and resolution do not allow confident identification as a plasma cell. Leukocytosis is not appreciable in this field. The rouleaux supports a paraproteinemia, and in the given clinical context the findings are suggestive of a plasma cell neoplasm such as plasma cell leukemia; higher-power review and a quantitative plasma cell count are required.

ddx.vs: Pseudo-rouleaux in thick areas disappears in the thin monolayer, whereas true rouleaux persists where red cells should lie separately.
Agglutinates form irregular three-dimensional clumps rather than linear coin-stack chains.
LPL can also produce rouleaux but circulating cells are mainly small lymphocytes and plasmacytoid lymphocytes rather than plasma cells.
